title: Causal Pathway from Agentic Deployment to Novel Scenario Failure

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain addressing the biggest identified gap in AI safety evaluation: agentic systems encountering novel tool combinations and goal conflicts not covered by single-step benchmarks.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building an agentic evaluation testbed with tool use requires advanced infrastructure, multi-step task design, and significant engineering expertise beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Designing multi-step tasks with embedded failure points plus building tool-use infrastructure is a substantial engineering project well beyond 30 hours for beginners.

novelty.reasoning: Agentic evaluation is an extremely active area. Anthropic released Bloom (Dec 2025) for automated behavioral evaluations of agentic models. The COMPASS benchmark addresses long-horizon agentic reasoning. A benchmark for outcome-driven constraint violations in autonomous AI agents exists (arxiv 2512.20798). Multiple frameworks identify the gap between single-step and multi-step evaluation. The specific idea of building a minimal testbed measuring what fraction of failures standard single-step evals would miss is partially addressed by existing work, though more accessible student-level implementations remain scarce.
